brands.d: New York housewares maker founded by Sam and John Farber whose soft-grip Good Grips line, designed with Smart Design, made ergonomic utensils mainstream.
Trademark of Grace Manufacturing (brothers Richard and Jeff Grace) whose photo-etched woodworking rasps became the definitive kitchen zester and grater.
The Peugeot family's mill business (PSP since 1989) that made the first coffee mill in 1840 and the first tabletop pepper mill in 1874, with lifetime-guaranteed steel mechanisms.
Nantucket design house of inventor Tom David whose Magnum and Magnum Plus mills are built in Italy by Tre Spade after a 40-year collaboration.
Affoltern am Albis family firm founded by Alfred Neweczerzal that made tens of millions of Rex peelers before its 2020 sale to Victorinox.
Ibach knife maker famous for the Swiss Army knife; also makes kitchen knives and, since buying Zena in 2020, the Rex peeler.
Rikon im Tösstal family firm known for Duromatic pressure cookers and the featherweight Original Swiss Peeler launched in 1986.
Swiss gadget brand founded by Karl Zysset in Lyss with the onion chopper; later IDEO-designed tools; owned by DKSH.
Marktoberdorf metalware maker whose hook-handled stainless utensils for the Open Kitchen hanging system have been its sole business since 1993.
London houseware firm of twins Richard and Antony Joseph, begun with glass chopping boards and known for colourful space-saving tools.
Church Gresley pottery renamed by Tom Cash in 1901, maker of the cane-glazed mixing bowl and pudding basins; now a Rayware Group brand.

traditions.r: Central Mexico (Puebla, Oaxaca and basalt regions)
traditions.d: Hand-carving of tripod mortars and tejolote pestles from single blocks of vesicular basalt, continuing Aztec and Maya practice.
traditions.tech: Chiselled from one block of porous basalt; interior left rough so worn bubbles keep renewing the grinding surface
traditions.auth: Real basalt is porous, heavy and needs breaking in with rice; concrete imitations are smooth, lighter, shed grit and never season.

traditions.d: Making of glazed stoneware mortars with combed kushi-no-me ridges inside, paired with wooden surikogi pestles, for sesame, miso and tororo.
traditions.tech: Thrown bowl, exterior glazed, interior left unglazed and combed with radiating grooves before firing
traditions.mat: Stoneware clay, glaze; sansho or other wood pestle
traditions.auth: Unglazed combed interior in a ceramic body; plastic versions wear quickly and are not traditional.

notes: Shelf rebuilt as 14 tier kinds (6 old kinds carried over and merged: Spatula k28, Cooking spoon k30, Ladle k29, Grater k32, Colander k31, Pepper mill k34; 8 new: Tongs, Whisk, Peeler, Can opener, Mortar and pestle, Measuring cups and spoons, Mixing bowl, Rolling pin). Archetypes only where a named pattern exists: Rex peeler (Zena 1947), Kuhn Rikon Original Swiss Peeler (1986), OXO Good Grips Swivel Peeler as the single OXO archetype, Microplane rasp grater, Peugeot Z/Bistro (1874) and Peugeot Paris (1987), Unicorn Magnum, molcajete, suribachi, Mason Cash Cane (1901). Old OXO per-utensil SKUs collapsed: Good Grips kept as one archetype plus the brand-register entry; old Microplane box-grater SKUs folded into the Microplane archetype versions; old pepper-mill eBay source replaced with the Peugeot history page. Models limited to market-covering brands plus America's Test Kitchen / Reviewed / TechGearLab test winners (4–9 per kind); attribute variants (box/rasp/rotary, balloon/French/flat/Danish, Y vs swivel, chinois/spider/sieve, salt vs pepper, bottle opener) are types, not kinds. Grill tongs noted as a type cross-referenced to Outdoor cooking rather than listed. Left out: Cole & Mason, Cuisipro, Cuisinart, JK Adams brand pages (not retrieved this session, so no register entries; they appear only as model makers); Microplane year given as mid-1990s because retrieved pages do not confirm 1994; Unicorn founding year not confirmed; Rösle and Zyliss have no single iconic archetype so are register entries only. Oroshigane kept as a grater type. Spice racks, salad spinners, garlic presses and kitchen shears belong to other shelves per the plan.
